Ancestry: Gargoyle Heritage: Dhampir Class: Laughing Shadow Magus | Paradox of Opposites Seneschal Witch Age: 229 Backstory Mira had a very long life. Beginning as the unborn twin to her dhampiric sister, somehow not dead but really alive either. Lacking a body to call her own. A trapped soul. Oddly fitting, given their heritage. Mira's only escape from this non-existence was being cast upon a wall, as her sister's living shadow. They both descend from so called "psychic vampires" or so they heard, the magicks her sister gained later in life did nothing but reaffirm that, but it sure was an easy way to explain their circumstance. In a way, they could simply not be without one and the other. Maybe her sister had the literal brains but Mira was the mastermind behind their every move, her consciousness, guide to greater power and magical prowess. Her sister provided being in the moment, corporeal and much needed levity, for the two of them. It also helped that she was pretty to boot, very skilled at talking to people. They made a pretty great team, as best as they could manage, even if her beloved sister took all of the credit at times. Their hard earned work but she was fine for the longest time. That was until they fell hard for the same woman and Mira of course, let her sister take charge. To enjoy what she could never have but the sheet strain this put between them was something that tore them apart. Miriam certainly sought to make that literal, she had enough with having to "share" her every little joy, give it all away. It took a lot of pain, effort, blood, sweat, tears but also, reconciliation and negotiation. Mira and her sister had managed to sever themselves, one from the other, together as it turns out, as a team once more. A gradual process, as Miriam was granted a sad little familiar to embody at first but being corporeal outweighed anything making her uncomfortable. She even revealed herself to her sister's love afterwards and somehow, the three of them made it work. It all worked out in the end and Miriam became more and more real. Day by day, with both occult study, friendships earned and memories made, she gained a body all her own. She became more real than real. But as the years went on and on, her hunger for knowledge and magic was not satisfied, the spring in her step did not falter. Learning to do magicks all on her own, learning to do quite a lot without her sister actually, they sure had less and less time spent together as things moved forward, even less time to share with their wife. Why can't she remember their faces? They kept slowing down, trailing behind her.... By the time she had forgotten their names. The regret crushed her the most, things left unsaid, mistakes made over the decades, so much hurt, and yet. Mira could not stop in her pursuit for higher power by that point, it was all she had left. Alone. Diving into ancient, forbidden tome after forbidden tome. Making pacts with higher powers left and right. Looking at god right in the eye and asking them why? Why all this? -# All she ever wanted was to... Then, she blacked out, Mira can't remember when it happened exactly nor how but yes, she had woken up in unknown lands that she would later come to know as Ao . All Mira could recall was a blurry mess, the night prior. There was laughter though, so much laughter, cruel and wicked. A dreadful feeling that would not leave her, even now. She was lost here, but not alone, for Mira had come with a companion of sorts. A thing she has never known nor seen before but instinctually, she held onto her tiny paws, looked into those beady little eyes and silly little pink horn for a nose. Mira knew at that moment that she could not let go of her now. Her little Luz... She is not sure where the name came from exactly but it was comforting, somehow. The pair made their way forward henceforth. Together again. "Kobold!" 1:17 AM Uhh idk what other info to provide but i used player 229 to make both of their sheets. To close this press the close button TicketTool.xyz - Ticketing without clutter Taelyn 12 | Eva 12 | Bloop 12 6/3/2025 2:23 PM So Bal and I were looking over the rules for the Controlled Convergence Ritual. We both have some concerns about this that we want to bring up, so if you could, could Balf be added to this ticket? There are three main concerns we want to bring up. 1: Mechanics for a Meta function If this is a meta function of the game, does it actually even need an mechanical aspect to it? Why is it not just a pay and get it done situation? Is this just for the ritual guild? 2: The Ritual Failure Consequences On failure the current negatives essentially make martials unfun and dangerous to play for a very long period of time, while casters aren't as heavily affected. Even if you were to balance this out by adding, say stupefied, making characters affected in real time is unfun since... You're literally not playing the game. 3: The Lore/Flavor The idea of a the ritual being a intentionally created convergence is just... dumb. No one in their right mind would intentionally delete themselves to summon another version of themselves. When I did the mission, I assumed we were using what was learned to make a "new ritual" that isn't convergence based since it referenced research on ancestries and rituals. I think it is a mistake to flavor the ritual as a convergence since it not only insane to do, but it seems anathema to the entire goal of Axiom, to stop the convergences, not make new ones. Suggestions I doubt you will want to make it not a mechanical ritual, and that's okay, but we suggest that instead of it making your character near unplayable, it instead eats up downtime based on failure. (Example is 14 days on failure, 30 on crit-fail). Also the flavor should be changed to not be convergence based, or be unflavored, being flavored as the casters want. (edited) Iron 6/3/2025 3:05 PM 1: There was a long discussion about making this essentially risk free, but we ultimately decided that unlike the resurrection ritual, the reincarnate ritual is something you choose. You have to take a risk and you are choosing to do it. There needs to be a risk; The other option was an exorbitant cost. A risk makes sense in-universe too. Additionally we removed the crit fail condition, which would have been worse. 2: Again, you're choosing to remake yourself. Its a choice. There has to be a cost. This is to enable a higher level character to remake their build. You already get a free remake within your first five games, which is plenty of time to notice a glaring flaw. 3: Its worth noting you're still you. You aren't a different character. You've essentially bodyswapped and some of your early memories are different but you're still you. The reason we're doing this risky and forbidden ritual is because the threat is escalating, and desperate times call for desperate measures. As for why it uses convergences, they are a tool, albeit a dangerous one. We are fighting against uncontrolled convergences, but that doesn't mean the use of controlled convergences is anathema to use. The moral implications are up to your character. Its worth noting the ritual is not meant to be easy, simple, or morally uncomplicated. Unlike the concessions we made with the resurrection ritual, where we determined that death is something that happens to you, and if you want to reverse it you should be able to within reason, this ritual is a choice. If the implications are unappealing to you, you are free not to make that choice, and nothing bad will happen to you. What is the proper ruling on Alchemical Bombs and Shadow Sheath An alchemical bomb combines volatile components that explode when the bomb hits a creature or object. Most alchemical bombs deal damage, though some produce other effects. Bombs have the bomb trait. Bombs are martial thrown weapons with a range increment of 20 feet. When you throw a bomb, you make a weapon attack roll against the target's AC, as you would for any other weapon. It takes one hand to draw, prepare, and throw a bomb. The bomb is activated when thrown as a Strike—you don't have to activate it separately. As consumables, bombs can't have runes etched onto them, have talismans attached to them, or benefit from runes granted in other ways (such as from spells or from items that replicate runes from other items). Spells and magic items that give you a bonus to all your attacks (or to all thrown weapons, for example) can still apply to them. As long as the shadow sheath is on your person, you can Interact to draw an exact copy of the weapon from thin air. As it can be any ammunition, including arrows and crossbow bolts, the acceleration of the round is entirely separate from any features of the weapon that is firing it--thus, it is not accelerated by the weapon itself. Rather, the magnetic properties of the ammunition accelerate it when fired at a target wearing metal armor or made of metal. As such, I believe this ammunition is only supposed to work/have any effect against such targets. It is explicitly stated that the +1 circumstance bonus to hit only applies against targets wearing/made of metal, while for the increased damage effect, it is simply stated that "Due to magnetic acceleration, the ammunition deals more damage and has deadlier critical hits, also according to its type." As previously established, this magnetic acceleration is not due to a property of the weapon firing it, instead being caused by the target attracting the ammunition towards it, thus making it dependent on the target fulfilling the same criteria as explicitly laid out for the +1 circumstance bonus to hit. The exact RAW wording of this is somewhat unclear on this, but I believe this to be RAI. It is a minor issue, but one that I believe should be addressed. To close this press the close button TicketTool.xyz - Ticketing without clutter Krax - Soot 11/Tess 6/Juniper 4 11/27/2025 1:41 PM Could we get an official ruling on how to interpret the Fracture Mountains (transcend) from Titan’s Breaker? We had this discussion unofficially before and at least there it seems everyone agreed on the stronger reading. I’m considering building around it to some degree and I would actually need to adjust the foundry rule element depending on the ruling. So I’d like an official thing I could point to. Explanation: Titan’s Breaker is an exemplar weapon icon and has an immanence (passive) effect: "The titan’s breaker deals 2 additional spirit damage per weapon damage die to creatures it Strikes.” * The 2 action Fracture Mountains (Transcendence) reads: *“Make a melee Strike with the titan’s breaker. This counts as two attacks when calculating your multiple attack penalty. If this Strike hits, your additional spirit damage from the ikon’s immanence increases to 4 plus an extra die of weapon damage . If you’re at least 10th level, it’s increased to 6 spirit damage and two extra dice, and if you’re at least 18th level, it’s increased to 8 spirit damage and three extra dice.” 1:41 PM You can read this in two ways: a) Your immanence increases to 4 per weapon damage die , plus an extra die of weapon damage => A 2d6 weapon would add 8 +1d6 damage => Even this rarely does as much damage as a Fighter default Striking twice and is usually worse. => I believe this to be the RAI and balanced option. b) Your immanence increases to 4 flat , plus an extra die of weapon damage. => A 2d6 weapon would add 4 +1d6 damage => This would essentially just turn it into a worse Power Attack on most levels because it moves your Spark and the flat damage is equal to your normal passive immanence damage you’d have even without transcending. All you’d gain by transcending is one weapon damage die. => This is the option foundry defaults to. There is some discussion online but no consensus really. For a ruling I could suggest: "Transcendence — Fracture Mountains is to be read as “If this Strike hits, your additional spirit damage from the ikon’s immanence increases to 4 per weapon damage die plus an extra die of weapon damage.” 1:44 PM Bonus neurospicy graph Ozrin 12/ Koltek 12/ Laev 8 11/27/2025 2:26 PM I think 4 per damage die is the correct reading 2:26 PM without that, it becomes a much more niche transcend, really only useful against objects Krax - Soot 11/Tess 6/Juniper 4 11/27/2025 2:27 PM Yeah, 4 flat would be too bad to be true essentially.
